title: KV shadow reservation and prefetch admission controller to reduce fragmentation under bursty tenants
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: During bursty, multi-tenant workloads we observe high KV cache fragmentation and prefill storms that increase p99 prefill latency and cause poor reuse. This ticket proposes a two-part runtime mechanism: (1) a lightweight 'shadow reservation' allocator that maintains small guarded allocations to reduce micro-fragmentation and enable fast coalescing; (2) a prefetch admission controller that scores incoming prefill requests using tenant burstiness, sequence-length histogram, kernel-affinity score, and current fragment map, then decides to admit, throttle, or defer prefill to a background wave. The goal is to reduce decode stalls and eviction churn without sacrificing tail latency for latency-sensitive tenants.
implementation_notes:
Design summary:
- Shadow reservation allocator: reserve N small shadow blocks per shard (configurable by tenant weight). These blocks act as sticky anchors so that adjacent small fills are coalesced instead of scattering fragments. Shadow blocks are managed with generational leases: if not used after X windows they are reclaimed.
- Prefetch admission controller: compute a realtime admission score = alpha * burst_score + beta * seq_length_penalty + gamma * kernel_affinity + delta * fragment_cost. admission thresholds are per-tenant and adaptive using EWMA of recent prefill success rate.
- Kernel selection integration: admission controller consults kernel-affinity that indicates whether a prefilling pattern will benefit from fused attention kernels vs tiled kernels; low-affinity prefetches are deprioritized to avoid wasted KV writes that are expensive to evict.
- Eviction & compaction: introduce micro-compaction pass that runs opportunistically during low GPU utilization to merge small neighboring fragments into compact slabs. Evictions prefer least-value fragments by combining access recency with predicted reuse score (from prefix-match heuristics).
- Prefill/decode scheduling: if admission decides to defer, requests are placed on a background decode wave with lower GPU priority and batched aggressively; admitted prefill runs on the normal fast path with KV write-through semantics.
- Telemetry: expose fragment histogram, shadow-reserve utilization, admission-decision breakdown, and decode-wave latencies.
Trade-offs and rationale:
- Shadow reservations increase reserved capacity but reduce fragmentation and repeated write/evict cycles; ideal for long-lived prefixes. We tune the reservation size per-tenant by weight to keep overall effective cache utilization high.
- Admission scoring requires tuning (alpha..delta). We will run offline sims and a staged rollout (canary tenants) before wide rollout.
- Kernel-affinity signals come from model profiling (sequence lengths & attention pattern). Integration requires mapping from model variant to kernel profiles.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Synthetic workload sims show >=30% reduction in small-fragment count and >=20% reduction in prefill-triggered evictions compared to baseline.
2) End-to-end p99 prefill latency for latency-sensitive tenants does not regress (>5% allowed).
3) Background decode wave reduces GPU stall time under bursty arrival patterns by >=15%.
4) Observability: fragment histogram, admission decisions, and shadow reserve utilization are visible in Console dashboards and logs.
5) Feature flags to disable shadow reservations or controller behavior per-tenant are available before rollout.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Over-reservation could reduce effective cache capacity and increase costs. Mitigation: start with conservative default reservations and per-tenant caps; monitor overall hit-rate and adjust.
Risk: Admission policy wrongly defers critical low-latency requests. Mitigation: request metadata includes latency_sensitivity flag; such requests bypass deferral.
Risk: Kernel-affinity signals stale for model variants. Mitigation: tag model versions with profiling artifacts and fall back to safe defaults.
